title: Email Queue + Retry Policy + Bounce Handling
head: d601fdd34
scope: Audit email queue config, retry policy, bounce handling, rate-limit/per-recipient throttle, DoS exposure, monitoring, sentinel coverage for transactional email (order confirmation/status, delivery-boy, password reset, verification, subscriber broadcast).
verdict_rationale: Structural email-infrastructure gaps are real but currently LATENT for V1 LOCAL Le Cayenne. ALL 5 Mailables (OrderMail, OrderGotMail, ResetPassword, SubscriberMail, VerifyEmail) declare the `Queueable` trait but DO NOT implement `ShouldQueue` at the class signature level — they send SYNCHRONOUSLY via SMTP inside the originating request, blocking the FPM worker for the round-trip. VerifyEmail imports `Illuminate\Contracts\Queue\ShouldQueue` at file level but the `class VerifyEmail extends Mailable` line does not carry `implements ShouldQueue` — same dead-import pattern as SendResetPasswordNotification listener (verified via dedicated sentinel test, second-pass correction of initial audit). All 5 listeners that wrap `Mail::to()->send()` swallow exceptions to `Log::info` (not Log::error, not Log::critical, not failed_jobs) — so SMTP outages are invisible to any pager grep, no retry occurs, no admin alert fires. Zero bounce-handling infrastructure (no Mailgun webhook route, no `users.bounced_at` column, no suppression list, no `Queue::failing()` handler in EventServiceProvider). Supervisor template only watches `--queue=high,default` — even if Mailables WERE made `ShouldQueue`, they would land on `default` and starve behind `DispatchDomainEventsJob` on `high`. No dedicated `mail` lane. NO per-recipient throttle exists (e.g. password-reset spam protection lives only in `ForgotPasswordController`-level rate limit, not at the mail-dispatch layer). BLAST RADIUS LIMITED BECAUSE: (a) `OrderMailNotificationBuilder::send()` early-returns for `source == 10` (Kiosk Machine) — kiosks dominate V1 traffic so customer-email path is rarely walked; (b) `.env` ships `MAIL_HOST=` empty and `MAIL_PORT=0` — Mail::send fails fast (TCP refused) before adding observable latency, and the silent Log::info catch makes that failure invisible to the request path. The structural risk MATERIALIZES when owner configures real MAIL_HOST (Mailgun/SES) AND web/mobile-app order volume grows past ~kiosk-dominated mix. Verdict matches J-ADV-5 D7 P1 vector pattern: V1 LOCAL deferable, V1 LIVE-PROD/V2 SaaS becomes critical.

supervisor_workers.mail_lane_resolution_today: ALL Mailables that ARE queueable would dispatch onto 'default' (no ->onQueue('mail') override anywhere in app/Mail or listeners). 'default' is shared with non-priority outbox tail + ad-hoc jobs.

worker_level.applies_to: Failed dispatch of QUEUED jobs (NONE today for Mailables — all 5 Mailables are synchronous via dead-import or missing implements). Applies to actually-queued non-mail jobs: DispatchDomainEventsJob, SendFcmNotificationJob, ProcessWebhookEventJob, SloEvaluatorJob.
worker_level.backoff_strategy: NONE — `--backoff` flag absent from queue:work invocation. Failed retries fire immediately (Laravel default 0s when no $backoff on job).

retry_policy.mailable_level_backoff: No $backoff property defined on any Mailable in app/Mail/. Compare app/Jobs/DispatchDomainEventsJob.php which defines $backoff=[1,5,15,60,300] tries=6. Email retry curve is therefore linear-zero (3 attempts back-to-back) — bad shape against transient SMTP timeouts which need exponential decay.

synchronous_mail_failures.behavior: NO RETRY whatsoever. Try/catch in listener body → Log::info($e->getMessage()) → silent return.
examples: SendResetPasswordNotification.php:34-36 catches Exception → Log::info (INFO level — invisible to ANY grep for warn/error/critical)
synchronous_mail_failures.impact: SMTP outage → ZERO retry, ZERO failed_jobs entry, ZERO pager signal, ZERO admin notification. Customer never receives password reset / order confirmation. Operator never knows.

permanent_failure_admin_notification.evidence_searched: grep -rn 'Queue::failing|Bus::failing' app/Providers — zero matches. AppServiceProvider.php and EventServiceProvider.php both checked.
permanent_failure_admin_notification.recommendation: Add `Queue::failing(function (JobFailed $event) { ... })` in EventServiceProvider::boot or AppServiceProvider::boot. Pipe to `Log::channel('fiscal')->critical(...)` (re-use existing nightly grep pipeline established by EscalateOutboxBroadcastSwallowed pattern).

bounce_handling.evidence: grep -rn 'MailgunWebhook|mail.*bounce|webhook.*mail' app/Http/Controllers routes — ONLY hit is config/services.php mailgun stanza (provider config only, no inbound webhook handler). routes/api.php + routes/web.php inspected: zero `/webhook/mailgun/*` or `/webhook/ses/*` routes.

users_table_bounce_columns.bounced_at: NOT PRESENT — grep migrations for `bounce` returned zero hits in users table schema

bounce_handling.suppression_list: NONE. No `email_suppressions` table. No middleware-level skip-if-bounced check before Mail::to(). One bounced address would receive every subsequent email forever, accumulating provider-side reputation damage.
bounce_handling.complaint_handling: NONE (FBL spam complaints, Mailgun `complained` webhook, AWS SES `Complaint` SNS event — all unhandled).
bounce_handling.impact: If owner configures Mailgun in production and ships even one campaign via SubscriberMail to a stale list: hard-bounce rate >5% will rate-limit the sending domain on Mailgun side, soft-bounce loop will keep retrying forever (no retry cap at app layer because mail is synchronous and not queued). Sender-reputation degradation is permanent on shared Mailgun pools.

rate_limiting.mailgun_provider_caps: Free tier: 5 messages/sec, 100/day post sandbox. Flex tier: 60k/month. Paid: per-plan throttling. App-level enforcement: ZERO.

per_recipient_throttle.evidence: No `cache->throttle()` / `RateLimiter::attempt()` keyed by recipient email anywhere in app/Listeners or app/Services Mail builders. Compare app/Listeners/NotifyStockLowOnStockLevelChanged.php:29-56 which DOES throttle per-key (good template). Email path has nothing equivalent.
per_recipient_throttle.concrete_risk: Order status state machine can flip a single order through PENDING→ACCEPT→PREPARING→PREPARED→OUT_FOR_DELIVERY→DELIVERED within minutes (KDS bump-board taps). OrderMailNotificationBuilder fires on EVERY transition WITHOUT dedup → 6 emails to one customer for one order. Multiply by 50 orders/day.

rate_limiting.global_send_rate_caps: NONE. No Bus::batch chunking. No `dispatch()->delay()`. No throttle-per-minute around SubscriberMail broadcast.

password_reset_dispatch_throttle.evidence: ForgotPasswordController.php:53 dispatches without per-email cache check. Request-layer throttle (Laravel's named `password-reset` throttle) caps HTTP requests per IP, NOT per email destination — an attacker rotating IPs can still spam mailbox of victim.
password_reset_dispatch_throttle.recommendation: Add per-email cache::add('reset-mail:'.sha1($email), 1, 60) gate in SendResetPasswordNotification::handle before Mail::send.

order_confirmation_email_path.is_queued_today: Event SendOrderMail::dispatch() routes to listener SendOrderMailNotification (NOT ShouldQueue) → OrderMailNotificationBuilder::send() → Mail::to()->send() — fully SYNCHRONOUS
order_confirmation_email_path.kiosk_source_skip: OrderMailNotificationBuilder.php:33 — `if ($this->order->source == 10) return;` — Kiosk orders SKIP mail entirely. This is the primary reason V1 latency exposure is low TODAY.
order_confirmation_email_path.web_app_path: Web app orders (source != 10) fall through to synchronous Mail::send. With empty MAIL_HOST in current .env, request fails fast (TCP refused) and Log::info swallows. Once MAIL_HOST is populated in production, customer-facing latency on web ORDER CREATE POST = SMTP round-trip (typ. 200ms-2s).

password_reset_email_path.is_queued_today: Event → listener SendResetPasswordNotification (imports ShouldQueue but does NOT implement it) → Mail::to()->send(new ResetPassword(...)) — SYNCHRONOUS
password_reset_email_path.customer_facing_latency_impact: Once MAIL_HOST populated: ForgotPassword POST blocks for SMTP round-trip + retry-zero-on-failure. Slow Mailgun = slow forgot-password page.

verification_email_path.is_queued_today: Framework's SendEmailVerificationNotification listener implements ShouldQueue (Laravel default) — but the app-side VerifyEmail Mailable does NOT implement ShouldQueue (dead-import). The framework listener queues itself onto 'default'; when the worker picks it up it then calls `notify(new VerifyEmailNotification)` which sends via Mail::send synchronously WITHIN THE QUEUE WORKER PROCESS. Net effect: SMTP latency moves off the FPM thread but the worker thread blocks per-recipient. Better than fully-sync, worse than per-recipient queued mail. Per-job timeout is 120s (--timeout=120) so a hung SMTP would burn one worker slot for up to 2min before SIGTERM.

email_queue_dos.j_adv_5_reference: phase-j/J-ADV-5-dos-findings.json — email queue not covered in D1-D15 (notification path = FCM SendFcmNotificationJob only, mail path absent)
email_queue_dos.unbounded_growth_vector: If Mailables WERE made ShouldQueue (currently they're not), they would land on 'default' queue alongside outbox + ad-hoc jobs. Worker `--max-jobs=1000` cycles every 1000 jobs but does NOT cap queue DEPTH — only worker process recycling. A 50k-recipient SubscriberMail broadcast would queue 50k jobs onto Redis. With numprocs=2 and ~200ms/SMTP-job → drain rate ~10 mail/sec → 50k mail = ~83min drain (acceptable in isolation) BUT shares lane with kiosk/POS-critical outbox dispatches.
email_queue_dos.current_blast_radius_zero_because: Mail is NOT queued today — DoS vector doesn't exist via redis queue. It exists via FPM worker pool starvation: a SubscriberMail::send loop over N recipients with synchronous Mail::send blocks the originating PHP-FPM worker for N × SMTP round-trip. With pm.max_children typical 8-16 on VPS-1 (4GB RAM), one operator clicking 'send to 1000 subscribers' wedges the admin request thread for ~3min.
email_queue_dos.redis_eviction_safety: Redis maxmemory-policy=allkeys-lru does NOT touch list keys (Laravel queue uses LPUSH/RPOP) — queue jobs are safe under memory pressure (per J-ADV-5 D14).

Plus assertion that supervisor template watches expected lanes + failed_jobs infrastructure intact + listener dead-import baseline + VerifyEmail dead-import baseline. Sentinel value: catch silent drift either direction.

top_3_concerns: Synchronous Mail::to()->send() in 4 of 5 listener paths + Log::info exception swallowing → SMTP outages invisible to pager, zero retry, zero failed_jobs trail. Currently latent because MAIL_HOST=empty and kiosk source=10 skips mail. Materializes immediately when owner configures real MAIL_HOST AND web-app order volume grows.

Zero bounce-handling infrastructure (no Mailgun/SES webhook route, no users.bounced_at column, no suppression list, no FBL complaint handling). One stale subscriber list shipped via SubscriberMail = permanent sender-reputation damage on shared Mailgun pools.

Supervisor template watches --queue=high,default ONLY — even if Mailables WERE made ShouldQueue, they would land on 'default' alongside DispatchDomainEventsJob outbox tail and ad-hoc jobs. No dedicated mail lane. Order-critical outbox dispatch could be starved by a 50k SubscriberMail broadcast.
production_monitoring_recommendations: Queue::failing global handler in EventServiceProvider::boot piping to Log::channel('fiscal')->critical — re-uses nightly grep pipeline (no new infra). Fixes observability gap for ALL queued jobs, not just mail.
Mail queue depth alert (Redis LLEN 'queues:default' OR 'queues:mail' post lane split) via hourly artisan cron with threshold N=100 → admin email/dashboard alert.
Bounce rate dashboard panel in admin/observability/mail (blocked on Mailgun webhook handler — prerequisite work). Until then: link out to Mailgun dashboard for sender reputation monitoring.
failed_jobs admin observability page filtering by payload LIKE '%App\\Mail\\%' to surface mail-specific permanent failures distinct from outbox/FCM failures.
